case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed the placement of the child with his out-of-state father and the dismissal of the CHINS case, holding DCS's reunification efforts were reasonable and did not violate the statutory reasonable-efforts provision.
key_cases.relevance: Applies Indiana's statutory reasonable-efforts requirement to the services ordered during a CHINS case.
key_cases.quote: In light of the circumstances, we believe DCS's reunification efforts were reasonable.

key_cases.holding: The court vacated the judgment terminating the mother's parental rights because the CHINS court found her indigent and entitled to counsel but never appointed one, and those defective CHINS proceedings flowed directly into the termination action.
key_cases.relevance: Court-ordered service plans entered without the counsel a parent was found entitled to cannot support later termination.
key_cases.quote: J.A. was denied her statutory right to counsel during the course of the CHINS proceedings below and those proceedings flowed directly into an action to terminate her parental rights

key_cases.case_name: F.T. v. Indiana Department of Child Services
key_cases.holding: The court vacated the parental participation decree entered against an alleged father, holding that paternity must be established first and that the statutory prerequisites, including a proper verified participation petition, must be met before a juvenile court has authority to order parental participation as part of a CHINS disposition.
key_cases.relevance: Holds that a court-ordered service and participation decree is void for want of authority unless the verified petition and hearing requirements of Ind. Code 31-34-16 are satisfied first.
key_cases.quote: Because the proper procedures were not followed here, the juvenile court did not have authority to order F.T.'s parental participation as part of its CHINS disposition.
